recent_posts.title: When To Kill A Project
recent_posts.summary: Dave Verwer, creator of iOS Dev Weekly and Swift Package Index, shares lessons from 30 years of building software projects. Through case studies of both successes and failures—including the iOS Dev Survey that flopped despite massive effort, Tackle Fishing app that ignored market research, AppReviewTimes that solved a real problem until Apple fixed it, and the thriving Swift Package Index—he demonstrates critical skills for indie developers: knowing when to kill projects, conducting proper market research, focusing resources on what works, and recognizing when success means shutting down. The piece emphasizes that even experienced builders face failures, but long-term success comes from quickly identifying what isn't working and moving on.

recent_posts.title: The Great Connection Pool Meltdown
recent_posts.summary: Tuist's caching server experienced cascading failures when their cloud provider's network issues caused connection pool exhaustion. Thousands of failed S3 requests queued up, consuming memory until the server crashed repeatedly. The team implemented fail-fast queue configurations and migrated to a new provider (Render.com), resolving the stability issues. Key lessons include the importance of monitoring, trusting initial diagnoses, and designing systems that gracefully handle failures rather than cascading them.

recent_posts.title: Going full time as an indie creator with a 100 day deadline
recent_posts.summary: An iOS developer announces his transition to full-time indie content creation, setting a 100-day goal to reach £50k ARR through his tech publication. The strategy focuses on growing the subscriber base through new content formats like developer interviews and creator spotlights, while improving paid conversion rates by developing tools for iOS developers. Success means sustainable independence; failure means returning to traditional employment.

recent_posts.title: Newsletter referral program offers free subscriptions for sharing
recent_posts.summary: A tech blogger announces referral and gift programs to grow their newsletter subscriber base. Free subscribers can earn paid memberships by referring friends, with rewards ranging from 1 free month for 1 referral to a full year for 20 referrals. Paid subscribers can earn free months by sharing their gift subscriptions and converting recipients to paid plans. The post explains the mechanics of both programs and emphasizes the value proposition of weekly paid content versus bi-weekly free content.

recent_posts.title: Impostor Syndrome and Business Acumen
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the author's journey in monetizing his writing hobby, reflecting on imposter syndrome. He describes a pricing strategy adaptation for his paid subscription model, offering early access and exclusive content to subscribers. Upcoming changes to subscription rates are announced, with incentives to subscribe before the price hike, including discounts for certain groups.

recent_posts.title: README.md (new readers start here!)
recent_posts.summary: Jacob's Tech Tavern offers in-depth articles about iOS, Swift, and indie projects. The articles cover a wide range of topics including CPU architecture, tech hiring, compilers, startup fundraising, and the history of animation APIs. Jacob's approach to blogging is focused on solving interesting problems and learning new techniques. Some of his finest works include stories about indie projects, deep dives into Swift, tutorials on iOS development, and explanations of chip architecture transitions and fundraising experiences.

recent_posts.title: Async Unit Testing: The Comprehensive Guide
recent_posts.summary: This post provides a comprehensive guide on performing async unit testing in Swift, including handling unstructured concurrency. It covers topics such as using expectations, leveraging mocks, and handling conditions before assertions in async tests.

recent_posts.title: High Performance Swift Apps
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the performance optimization process for a Swift app called Check 'em - The Based 2FA App. The biggest performance bottleneck is the processing of TOTP codes and their 'interestingness'. The post suggests replacing regexes with more efficient algorithms and introducing parallelism to the TOTP calculation process. It also highlights the importance of fetching accounts and generating codes early in the app launch.
